key_insight: In d⁴ ruthenium Mott insulators, competition between triplet bandwidth and the singlet–triplet gap can produce excitonic magnetism, while lattice geometry and chemical bonding can instead favor valence bond solids.
engineering_relevance: The review informs quantum magnetic materials design through structural connectivity and bonding control, rather than AI or solar-cell engineering.
method: Review representative ruthenium compounds across four Ru–ligand octahedral connectivities.
Map compounds onto the conceptual ratio of triplet bandwidth to effective singlet–triplet gap.
Compare competing effects of spin–orbit coupling, exchange, hopping, crystal fields and covalency.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a comparative review spanning isolated octahedra, corner-sharing perovskites, edge-sharing honeycombs and corner-sharing pyrochlores, without reporting quantitative evaluation metrics.
watch_item: The bandwidth-to-gap ratio is a conceptual guide, not a sufficient predictor of the ground state when geometry and bonding favor competing phases.
paper_title: Excitonic magnetism and competing valence bond solid instabilities in $d^4$ ruthenium compounds
